headline: Russian backdoors found in 279 Slovak traffic cameras: SMS-triggered shell access and passwordless live feeds exposed.
summary: Slovakia's €30M EU-funded traffic camera rollout is halted after 279 NERO R-ONE units were found to contain SMS-activated Russian backdoors and passwordless live feeds. The system has been deactivated.
details: Slovakia's national security service, the NBU, discovered multiple security issues in 279 new NERO R-ONE speed cameras, part of a €30 million EU-funded modernization. These include SMS-activated Russian backdoors and passwordless access to live feeds. The system has since been deactivated.

The NERO R-ONE cameras are believed to be rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M units, produced by a St. Petersburg-based firm called Semicon. Their acquisition reportedly involved a Cyprus-based shell company with fake certifications.

The most critical finding is a hardcoded list of Russian phone numbers that can open shell and network access via SMS. Additionally, the SecureBoot feature is ineffective, and the web management portal exposes live streams to anyone with the camera's IP.

The Slovak Ministry of the Interior has deactivated all installed cameras. An independent auditor will verify the NBU's findings, and other Eastern European countries like Croatia may face similar issues with traffic control cameras of comparable origin.

headline_marked: [[DeepSeek-v4-flash-vision-exp now accepts images]] for multimodal AI tasks
headline: DeepSeek-v4-flash-vision-exp now accepts images for multimodal AI tasks
summary: The DeepSeek-v4-flash-vision-exp model now supports image inputs, allowing it to describe pictures, read text from screenshots, and analyze charts. It offers three methods for image provision, including direct embedding and file API uploads.
details: DeepSeek-v4-flash-vision-exp has been updated to accept images alongside text, enabling users to perform multimodal AI tasks. This includes describing pictures, extracting text from screenshots, and analyzing charts. The model supports common image formats such as JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP.

Developers can provide images to the model using three distinct methods, all compatible with the standard OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions format. These methods are also available through the Responses API, where images are carried in input_image content parts.

The first option is to encode the image as a base64 data URL and embed it directly in the request. This is straightforward for local files, but the encoded data contributes to a 48 MiB request body limit. Alternatively, a publicly accessible http(s) link can be provided, with the model downloading the image; this method has a 8192-character URL limit, a 32 MiB image file limit, and a 60-second download timeout.

The third and most flexible method involves uploading an image once via the Files API and then referencing its file_id in subsequent requests. This is ideal for reusing images or when image sizes exceed inline limits, as Files API images can be up to 64 MiB and are not subject to the 48 MiB request body constraint.

Images are converted into tokens based on their dimensions, with a maximum of 384 tokens per image regardless of size beyond a certain threshold. This token count is billed alongside text tokens. The model also supports an optional 'detail' field for image_url inputs to control processing.

In addition to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, DeepSeek-v4-flash-vision-exp can also receive images through the Anthropic-compatible /messages endpoint. This broad compatibility ensures developers can integrate the multimodal capabilities into various existing AI workflows.
